Sunlight catches reflective, rippling water between dense blocks of a compact Copenhagen-style canal district. Stepped pale stone, dark timber retaining walls, and iron railings define rectangular waterways beside narrow cobblestone streets.

Roughly thirty attached four- to six-storey townhouses form continuous street and canal-front rows. Slender façades in weathered muted red, mustard yellow, dusty blue, warm grey, beige, and exposed brick carry repetitive white-framed windows, arched doors and carriage entrances, and modest cornices. Steep tiled roofs, red, orange, and charcoal, are crowded with dormers and brick chimneys. Occasional exposed party walls show between staggered building rows.

A principal waterfront street follows the stone quay. Smaller streets cross it and connect over the canals by short, gently arched stone-and-metal bridges, one opening onto a broad paved promenade with rounded landings. Regularly spaced leafy trees, ornate black lamps, stone bollards, benches, European road signs, and zebra crossings furnish the district. Puddles, grime, and sparse weeds weather its sunlit surfaces.
